merger_description:
MedHealth Pty Ltd (**MedHealth**) proposes to acquire the business and assets of Integrity Medico-Legal Pty Ltd (**Integrity Medico-Legal**) pursuant to a business sale and purchase agreement (the **Acquisition**).

MedHealth is an Australian subsidiary of the US-based ExamWorks Group, which provides health and injury claim services and related services.  

Integrity Medico-Legal is an Australian company providing independent medical assessments, medico-legal assessments, reports, advice and related services.

Integrity Medico-Legal operates from a single premise at 11 Abbotsford Road, Bowen Hills QLD 4006 and provides services nationally, including via telehealth, with the majority of its revenue generated in Queensland and smaller proportions generated in Tasmania and the ACT.

Both MedHealth and Integrity Medico-Legal supply claim services related to health and injury, principally medico-legal assessments and independent medical assessments. MedHealth also supplies claims management and rehabilitation and return to work services among other things.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application and had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not be
likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information provided, given:
a. there is a horizontal overlap between MedHealth and
Integrity Medico-Legal in the supply of claim services
related to health and injury in Australia, including
medico-legal assessments and independent medical
assessments
b. the scope of the relevant markets is unclear and the
extent to which the merged entity is likely to be
constrained by alternative suppliers is uncertain
c. while the increment in MedHealth’s share of supply of
claim services related to health and injury arising from
the Acquisition is expected to be low, it may not
accurately reflect the potential competition effects of
the Acquisition given the uncertainty about market
definition and industry dynamics
d. MedHealth appears to be active across various
segments in the medical services industry and there is
insufficient information to determine that the Acquisition
would not be likely to raise material vertical or
conglomerate competition issues.
The ACCC considers that these potential competition issues would
be more appropriately considered through the notification process,
including via consultation with third parties.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
Considering the information provided by the parties, the ACCC
considers that there is a low likelihood of the Acquisition meeting
the thresholds for notification.
However, as the ACCC has been unable to reach a view that the
Acquisition would not be likely to raise competition issues, the ACCC
has determined not to make the notification waiver determination
applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
